subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: In hybridoma technology for monoclonal antibody production, which agent is commonly used to fuse B-cells with myeloma cells?
options: Polyethylene glycol (PEG)
Sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS)
Ethidium bromide
Restriction endonuclease
questions.explain: Polyethylene glycol (PEG) is a fusogen used to facilitate the fusion of plasma membranes between B-cells and myeloma cells to form hybridomas.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: What is the specific function of the HAT (Hypoxanthine-Aminopterin-Thymidine) medium in hybridoma selection?
options: It promotes the growth of myeloma cells.
It kills unfused B-cells.
It allows only fused hybridoma cells to survive by blocking the de novo nucleotide synthesis pathway.
It stimulates antibody production.
questions.explain: Aminopterin in HAT medium blocks the de novo nucleotide synthesis pathway. Myeloma cells lack the salvage pathway enzyme (HGPRT) and die. Unfused B-cells die naturally. Only hybridomas (which have HGPRT from the B-cell) can use Hypoxanthine and Thymidine via the salvage pathway to survive.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key advantage of monoclonal antibodies over polyclonal antibodies?
options: They recognize multiple epitopes on an antigen.
They are produced by different B-cell clones.
They possess high specificity for a single epitope.
They are easier and cheaper to produce in initial stages.
questions.explain: Monoclonal antibodies are derived from a single clone of B-cells and therefore recognize a single, specific epitope on an antigen, providing high specificity and consistency.

questions.q: Chimeric monoclonal antibodies are distinguishable by the fact that:
options: They are 100% mouse-derived.
They have mouse variable regions and human constant regions.
They are 100% human-derived.
They contain only the antigen-binding CDR loops from mice.
questions.explain: Chimeric antibodies (suffix -ximab) typically consist of variable regions (antigen-binding domains) derived from a mouse (or other source) fused to human constant regions to reduce immunogenicity.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: In the production of mAbs, myeloma cells are HGPRT defective. Why is this trait essential?
options: It prevents them from producing their own antibodies.
It ensures they die in HAT medium unless fused with a B-cell.
It makes them immortal.
It increases the fusion efficiency.
questions.explain: HGPRT deficiency means myeloma cells cannot use the salvage pathway for nucleotide synthesis. When placed in HAT medium (which blocks the main synthesis pathway), unfused myeloma cells die. Only fusions with B-cells (which provide HGPRT) survive.
